result.summary: The incident is mis-leveled logging on an expected attachment validation path, not a broken import; lowering that recorder log to info matches aggregate behaviour and leaves the API unchanged. The change is still observability-only and blunts error tracking for every attachment not_found on import, not just cross-customer cases, without aligning other client not_found import failures.

problems.title: Error tracking silencing
problems.detail: Any attachment entity_not_found from resolveAttachments (missing id or wrong customer) is logged at info on 'Failed to import record', so integration mistakes may stop paging even though behaviour is unchanged.

problems.title: Inconsistent import logging policy
problems.detail: Author/customer entity_not_found and other validation errors still hit recordFailed at error, while only attachment entity_not_found is special-cased.

problems.title: Tests overclaim logging
problems.detail: The litest proves API outcomes only; info-level logging is covered solely by importRecorder.test.ts, not end-to-end import.

result.betterFix: Consider keying recordFailed log severity on error.category (e.g. NOT_FOUND → info) for all import client validation failures, or a Datadog exclusion on this message plus err.code, instead of an attachment-only special case.
